oidc_jwt.description: Brokered OIDC providers can be configured to allow client assertions to be re-used.
oidc_jwt.source: OpenID Connect identity providers - Allows client assertions to be re-used
oidc_jwt.note: Replay of the same client assertion is expected when this switch is enabled and should not be reported as a freshness bug.

oidc_jwt.description: Refresh token rotation can be enabled or skipped depending on realm/client policy configuration.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC auth flows - Refresh token rotation
oidc_jwt.note: Reuse of a refresh token may be by design when rotation is suppressed.

oidc_jwt.description: TOTP codes may be reusable within the valid time interval depending on OTP policy and implementation window.
oidc_jwt.source: OTP policies documentation
oidc_jwt.note: Short-window TOTP reuse can be expected behavior unless reusable-code policy forbids it.

oidc_jwt.description: Bearer access tokens are replayable within their lifetime unless additional sender-constraining or revocation mechanisms are used.
oidc_jwt.source: sso-protocols/con-oidc-auth-flows.adoc and threat/compromised-tokens.adoc
oidc_jwt.note: Do not report same-token reuse as a freshness violation for ordinary bearer-token use.

oidc_jwt.description: Brokered usernames may be lower-cased unless case-sensitive username is enabled.
oidc_jwt.source: Identity broker general configuration - Case-sensitive username
oidc_jwt.note: Case-only differences between sent and granted identity can be by design.

oidc_jwt.description: First broker login flow can create a new local user or link to an existing local account depending on email/username matching and configured authenticators.
oidc_jwt.source: First login flow documentation
oidc_jwt.note: Identity merges during first broker login may be expected workflow behavior rather than unintended principal collapse.

oidc_jwt.description: On first broker login, Keycloak does not automatically link an existing local account by default because that is considered a potential security hole.
oidc_jwt.source: identity-broker/first-login-flow.adoc
oidc_jwt.note: A refusal to auto-link or a prompt for verification is expected behavior, not an identity-binding bug.

oidc_jwt.description: When validating signatures from an external OIDC IdP via JWKS, Keycloak caches the provider public key for performance.
oidc_jwt.source: OpenID Connect identity providers - Validate Signatures
oidc_jwt.note: Immediately after trust rotation, transient acceptance of old keys may reflect cache behavior; only persistent acceptance after refresh is suspicious.

oidc_jwt.description: Admin changes to external OIDC identity provider issuer, JWKS URL, or validating key are expected to change which upstream tokens are trusted.
oidc_jwt.source: identity-broker/oidc.adoc
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag acceptance under the new admin-configured trust anchor as a vulnerability. Only acceptance of the old trust anchor after intended rotation and cache expiry is suspicious.

oidc_jwt.description: The requesting frontend client is not automatically added to the access token audience.
oidc_jwt.source: Audience support documentation
oidc_jwt.note: Missing client_id in aud is expected unless an audience mapper adds it.

oidc_jwt.description: Admin-initiated changes to clients, policies, issuer bindings, or trusted keys are expected to affect subsequent logins.
oidc_jwt.source: Client Policies and identity provider configuration documentation
oidc_jwt.note: A login succeeding under newly authorized configuration is by design; only stale acceptance of superseded configuration should be flagged.

oidc_jwt.description: External OIDC IdP public keys are cached for performance, so trust-anchor rotation may not take effect instantly.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC identity provider setting 'Validate Signatures' and key caching note
oidc_jwt.note: Immediate acceptance of an old key right after admin rotation can be cache behavior; only persistent acceptance after refresh is suspicious.

oidc_jwt.constraint: Authorization endpoint tests MUST treat /realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/auth as a redirecting browser endpoint. Do NOT follow redirects automatically when testing request-object, state, nonce, or kc_idp_hint behavior; capture the 302/Location and callback parameters explicitly.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC URI endpoints and auth flows documentation

oidc_jwt.constraint: exchange_code_for_token and token_exchange requests to /realms/{realm}/protocol/openid-connect/token MUST use application/x-www-form-urlencoded parameters. JSON bodies are not the documented format and will cause false failures.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC URI endpoints and auth flows documentation

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 code-reuse tests, authorization codes are one-time and short-lived by design. A valid replay test must reuse the SAME code in a second token request; obtaining a fresh code after config change is a different flow and not evidence of replay acceptance.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC auth flows - Authorization Code Flow

oidc_jwt.constraint: For PKCE tests, client setting pkceCodeChallengeMethod has sentinel semantics: blank = PKCE not required but still accepted if sent; S256 = PKCE required with S256; plain = PKCE required with plain. Never assume blank disables PKCE support; it only disables enforcement.
oidc_jwt.source: Basic configuration - PKCE method

oidc_jwt.constraint: For redirect_uri tests, Valid Redirect URIs use exact case-sensitive string matching by default, with wildcard support only at the end of the pattern. For I3 redirect mismatch tests, use exact registered URIs unless intentionally testing the documented trailing-wildcard behavior.
oidc_jwt.source: Basic configuration - Valid Redirect URIs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For multi-identity I4 tests, redirect URI constraints are not identity constraints. Do NOT vary redirect_uri across compared identities unless the test specifically targets redirect validation, or you may create false differences unrelated to principal binding.
oidc_jwt.source: Basic configuration - Valid Redirect URIs

oidc_jwt.constraint: When testing OIDC brokered login against an external IdP, configure the broker IdP Issuer field. Without it, issuer validation semantics are not established from the docs; with it, Keycloak validates issuer claims from the IDP responses against that configured value.
oidc_jwt.source: OpenID Connect identity providers - Issuer

oidc_jwt.constraint: When testing external OIDC IdP signature validation, Validate Signatures must be ON and either JWKS URL or Validating Public Key must be configured. If Validate Signatures is OFF, signature-based attacks such as attacker-key resigning are not meaningful because signature verification is intentionally disabled.
oidc_jwt.source: OpenID Connect identity providers - Validate Signatures / Use JWKS URL

oidc_jwt.constraint: For key-rotation coherence tests against external OIDC IdPs, Keycloak caches the public key of the external OIDC identity provider for performance. After rotating JWKS or validating key configuration, allow for cache refresh behavior before concluding stale-key acceptance; only acceptance of the OLD key after explicit rotation and cache refresh is suspicious.
oidc_jwt.source: OpenID Connect identity providers - Validate Signatures / Use JWKS URL

oidc_jwt.constraint: For client assertion replay tests on brokered OIDC providers, Allows client assertions to be re-used is a by-design switch. If enabled, replay of the same client assertion is expected and MUST NOT be flagged as an I2 vulnerability. Only test replay rejection when this option is disabled.
oidc_jwt.source: OpenID Connect identity providers - Allows client assertions to be re-used

oidc_jwt.constraint: For audience validation of federated client assertions and JWT authorization grants, Allows Client ID as audience for assertions changes the accepted audience semantics to the configured client ID instead of token-url/issuer-url. Tests must align the assertion aud with this setting or they will misclassify by-design behavior.
oidc_jwt.source: OpenID Connect identity providers - Allows Client ID as audience for assertions

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 freshness tests on JWT client authentication, Max expiration has sentinel semantics: default is 60 seconds if not changed; tokens older than this are rejected as too old. Use {{now_epoch}} and {{now_epoch_plus_N}}-style claims and keep assertion lifetime within the configured max expiration for control cases.
oidc_jwt.source: Confidential client credentials - Signed JWT issued by the client / Signed JWT with Client Secret

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, always run a control token request with a valid token in the same client configuration. Otherwise, LOGIN_FAILED may be caused by wrong client authentication method, missing client secret/assertion, or disabled grant type rather than time validation.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC auth flows and confidential client credentials documentation

oidc_jwt.constraint: For token exchange I5 tests, Standard Token Exchange must be enabled on the client before using token exchange. A rejection when the switch is disabled is expected setup failure, not evidence of proper audience or scope enforcement.
oidc_jwt.source: Basic configuration - Standard Token Exchange

oidc_jwt.constraint: For token exchange scope-escalation tests, Keycloak documents a client-policy executor that can enforce downscoping of exchanged tokens to scopes already present in the subject_token. If such a client policy is enabled, requesting broader scope is expected to fail or be reduced; do not flag this as inconsistent behavior.
oidc_jwt.source: Client scopes - Downscoping; Client Policies executors

oidc_jwt.constraint: For token exchange audience tests, use the audience parameter explicitly only in token exchange contexts. The docs note audience simulation is currently only supported for token exchange; using audience assumptions in other grants can produce false interpretations.
oidc_jwt.source: Evaluating client scopes documentation

oidc_jwt.constraint: For access-token audience tests, remember the frontend client itself is NOT automatically added to the access token aud claim. Do not expect aud to contain the requesting client_id unless an Audience or Audience Resolve mapper adds it.
oidc_jwt.source: Audience support documentation

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 audience tests, access token audiences are shaped by client roles, audience mappers, and requested optional client scopes. A missing audience may be due to absent role-scope intersection or omitted optional scope, not a validation bug. Configure the relevant client scope and role mappings before testing enforcement.
oidc_jwt.source: Audience support; Role scope mappings; Client scopes permissions

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 role/permission binding tests, roles in issued tokens are the intersection of user-assigned roles and the client's role scope mappings. Missing roles after login can be by design if Full Scope Allowed is OFF or scope mappings are limited.
oidc_jwt.source: Role mappings in the token; Role scope mappings

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 client-scope policy tests, client scope matching is by explicit configured scope names, not wildcard semantics. If multiple different scopes must pass the same test, omit the restrictive client-scope policy or configure all needed scopes explicitly; do not assume '*' semantics.
oidc_jwt.source: Client scope-based policy documentation

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 role-policy tests, role matching is by explicit selected realm/client roles. If multiple different identities need to satisfy the same policy, assign the relevant roles to each identity or use a different policy type; do not treat role names as pattern-matched values.
oidc_jwt.source: Role-based policy documentation

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I5 regex-policy tests, Regex Policy target claims support regex matching on token-derived attributes, including nested JSON paths and array indexes. This is a true regex matcher, unlike exact-match settings such as redirect URIs or many named selections elsewhere; keep these semantics distinct when generating tests.
oidc_jwt.source: Regex-Based Policy documentation

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I4 brokered-identity tests, Case-sensitive username has exact documented semantics: if disabled, the username from the identity provider is lower-cased when federating users; if enabled, the original username is kept for the federated identity, although local server usernames are always lower-case. Case-only differences can therefore be by design.
oidc_jwt.source: Identity broker general configuration - Case-sensitive username

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I4 first-login collision tests, automatic linking of an existing local account to an external IdP is intentionally guarded because it is a potential security hole. Tests that rely on silent auto-linking must explicitly configure the dangerous AutoLink-style first login flow; otherwise prompts or refusal to auto-link are expected.
oidc_jwt.source: First login flow documentation

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I4 multi-user collision tests on brokered login, if the first login flow uses Automatically Set Existing User or Detect Existing Broker User, account linking/selection behavior is flow-dependent. The fuzzer MUST keep the first-login flow constant across compared identities or it will misattribute admin-configured linking behavior to a principal-binding flaw.
oidc_jwt.source: First login flow documentation

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I3 config-change sequences, admin changes to trust anchors, issuer bindings, default IdP, first-login flow, post-login flow, or client policies are expected to affect NEW logins immediately. Only acceptance of OLD trust/config after explicit tightening or rotation is suspicious; success under the NEW admin-approved config is by design.
oidc_jwt.source: Identity provider configuration, client policies, and OIDC broker docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: For OIDC RP logout tests, if post_logout_redirect_uri is supplied then either client_id or id_token_hint must also be supplied, and the redirect URI must match a configured Valid Post Logout Redirect URI. Failures without these prerequisites are expected and not evidence of session-binding issues.
oidc_jwt.source: OIDC Logout - RP-Initiated Logout

oidc_jwt.constraint: For session/token lifetime tests, client-level timeout fields have sentinel semantics: if Client Offline Session Idle or Client Offline Session Max are not set, realm defaults are used; Access Token Lifespan, Client Session Idle, and Client Session Max override realm values when set. Do not assume unset means zero.
oidc_jwt.source: Advanced Settings for OIDC

oidc_jwt.constraint: For mTLS-bound token tests, sender-constrained tokens cannot be used as subject_token in standard token exchange. A token-exchange failure with an mTLS-bound subject_token is expected by design and must not be flagged as an audience/scope enforcement success or failure.
oidc_jwt.source: Advanced configuration - OAuth 2.0 Mutual TLS Certificate Bound Access Tokens Enabled

oidc_jwt.constraint: For organization-scope tests, the organization scope has exact documented request forms only: organization, organization:{alias}, and organization:*. Do not use wildcard-like aliases beyond the documented '*' form.
oidc_jwt.source: Mapping organization claims documentation

oidc_jwt.constraint: Authorization endpoint tests MUST preserve and bind state across the full browser flow. Keycloak creates authentication sessions and sub-sessions, and multi-tab/browser interactions can restart authentication automatically. For I3 state-swap or flow-coherence tests, compare the same request/session binding, not different browser tabs that legitimately restart auth.

Authorization code replay is BY DESIGN prevented: the temporary code in Authorization Code Flow cannot be used more than once. For I2/I3 tests involving code reuse, expect second exchange to fail and treat success as suspicious only if the exact same code is accepted twice.

For PKCE tests, client configuration controls enforcement. If client PKCE method is blank, Keycloak does not require PKCE, though clients may still use it. To test pkce_skip meaningfully, configure the client with attributes.pkce.code.challenge.method set to S256 or plain; otherwise omission of code_verifier is not evidence of a bug.

Valid Redirect URIs use exact case-sensitive string matching, with wildcard support only at the end of the pattern. For redirect_uri_mismatch and request-object parameter injection tests, do not assume prefix or case-insensitive matching. A literal '*' pattern allows any http/https redirect URI and would invalidate redirect-binding security tests.

For OIDC RP / external IdP validation tests, configure the identity provider Issuer field. Documentation states Keycloak validates issuer claims against this configured value. If issuer is omitted, issuer-comparison behavior is not guaranteed for the test setup, so I1 trust-anchor-substitution results may be inconclusive.

For OIDC RP signature-validation tests, set Validate Signatures=ON and configure either Use JWKS URL + JWKS URL or a static validating public key. If Validate Signatures is OFF, alg/key-substitution tests are invalid because Keycloak is configured not to verify external ID Token signatures.

When testing signing-key rotation for an external OIDC IdP, account for documented public-key caching. Keycloak caches the external IdP public key for performance. Only flag acceptance of the old key after an explicit trust rotation once the relevant cache has refreshed/expired; immediate post-rotation acceptance can be cache-related rather than an I3 failure.

For OIDC SSO audience-cross-tenant and cross-provider audience tests, configure distinct client IDs per provider/client and verify the external IdP configuration uses the intended Client ID. Keycloak documentation states the realm acts as an OIDC client to the external IdP, so audience validation must be interpreted relative to that configured client_id.

For client assertion replay tests against federated client authentication, note the provider setting 'Allows client assertions to be re-used'. By default, a client assertion cannot be used multiple times; enabling this option makes reuse accepted by design. Do not report replay acceptance as a vulnerability if this option is enabled.

For client assertion audience-binding tests, note the provider setting 'Allows Client ID as audience for assertions'. If enabled, Keycloak accepts the configured Client ID as the only valid audience instead of token-url/issuer-url, and documentation explicitly says this is non-standard. Tests must align expected audience with this setting or they will produce false positives.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, include a control login using a valid token/session in the same client/realm configuration. Keycloak has many client and realm timeout overrides; a failed attack login without a valid control cannot distinguish freshness enforcement from broken client configuration or disabled grant type.

Client session and token timeout fields have sentinel semantics. In WebAuthn policy, Timeout=0 means implementation-dependent/default browser/authenticator behavior, not immediate expiry. In password policy, Maximum Authentication Age=0 means always re-authenticate. In user session limits, max sessions value 0 means the check is disabled, not zero sessions allowed. Never treat 0 uniformly across Keycloak numeric fields.
Hashing iterations password policy has sentinel semantics: value -1 means use the algorithm default iteration count, not negative or disabled hashing. Do not assume -1 disables the check.

For token exchange scope-escalation tests, Keycloak provides a client-policy executor that can enforce downscoping of exchanged tokens to scopes already present in the subject_token/assertion. If this executor is enabled, rejection of expanded scope is by design. If it is not enabled, expanded scopes may reflect configuration rather than a core token-exchange bug; record whether downscope enforcement is configured.

For token exchange audience tests, use the token endpoint with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange and set audience explicitly. Documentation describes token exchange as the mechanism to obtain a token for another service audience; omitting audience can make the result ambiguous for I5 audience-binding checks.

Sender-constrained mTLS access tokens cannot be used as subject_token in standard token exchange. If the client has OAuth 2.0 Mutual TLS Certificate Bound Access Tokens enabled, do not use those tokens for token_exchange tests; rejection is by design.

Role scope mappings and client scopes intentionally limit token roles to an intersection of user roles and client-permitted scopes. For I5 authorization-binding tests, expected permissions must be computed as upstream user/service-account roles ∩ client role-scope mappings ∩ requested optional scopes, not simply all roles assigned to the user.

Client-scope policy semantics are OR by default unless a scope is marked Required, in which case all required scopes must be present. Group and role policies similarly support optional entries with required subsets. Authorization tests must model these semantics exactly or they will misclassify intended policy behavior as over-granting.

Regex-based policy target claims use Java regular expressions. Exact-match assumptions are invalid for those policy types. Conversely, many client and redirect URI fields are exact-match unless documentation explicitly mentions wildcard or regex support. Do not substitute '*' into exact-match fields expecting wildcard behavior.

For I4 multi-identity tests involving brokered usernames, Keycloak may lowercase brokered usernames unless 'Case-sensitive username' is enabled on the identity provider. If case-sensitive username is disabled, 'Admin' and 'admin' may intentionally collapse at the username layer; treat this as configuration-driven behavior, not necessarily a collision bug.

For organization and brokered-login tests, account linking and first-login flows can intentionally merge an external identity into an existing local account based on email/username plus configured authenticators. Cross-user identity merge findings are only meaningful if automatic linking/first-broker-login behavior is controlled and documented for the test.

The built-in organization scope is optional and must be requested as scope=organization, scope=organization:<alias>, or scope=organization:* to map organization claims into OIDC tokens. Absence of organization claims without the scope request is by design and must not be treated as authorization loss or identity confusion.

create_tenant returns 201/2xx with no body in typical Keycloak admin behavior; the realm name is the value supplied in the request, not a response field. Do not rely on response captures for the tenant identifier in subsequent steps.

For I2 replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti tests, do NOT treat repeated use of the same JWT bearer token as a vulnerability on Keycloak OIDC token validation by default. The documentation explicitly notes that access tokens are bearer tokens and discusses replay mitigation via short lifetimes, refresh handling, mTLS/DPoP, and revocation rather than one-time-use tracking.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against OIDC tokens, include a CONTROL login using a valid token/session in the same client/realm configuration. A failed attack request alone is ambiguous because client configuration, redirect URI, client authentication, or flow binding may be broken.

For I3 authorization-code replay tests, Keycloak documents that the temporary authorization code cannot be used more than once. Reuse the exact same code in a second token request to test replay resistance; do not confuse this with refresh-token behavior.

For PKCE-related tests, the client PKCE method setting has sentinel semantics: blank means PKCE is allowed but NOT required; S256 means PKCE is required with S256; plain means PKCE is required with plain. Never assume an unset PKCE method enforces PKCE.

For redirect_uri validation tests, Keycloak uses exact case-sensitive string matching for valid redirect URIs, except that wildcards are only allowed at the end of the configured pattern. For I3 redirect_uri_mismatch tests, use exact registered URIs unless intentionally testing the documented trailing-wildcard behavior.

For I1/I5 audience tests on access tokens, do not expect the frontend client_id to appear automatically in the access token aud claim. Keycloak documentation states the frontend client itself is not automatically added as audience. Configure audience via Audience or Audience Resolve mappers/client scopes before testing audience enforcement.

For I5 empty_audience and audience_mismatch tests, first configure audience-producing client scopes or role mappings. Without explicit audience configuration, absence of aud on an access token can be by design rather than an audience-validation flaw.

For I5 token_exchange_scope_escalation tests, Keycloak provides a client-policy executor that can enforce downscoping for token exchange, but this is not implied by default. The fuzzer must record whether downscope enforcement was configured; otherwise broader exchanged scopes may reflect missing hardening rather than a regression from an intended policy.

For I5 token_exchange_wrong_audience and token_exchange_ignore_audience tests, configure the target client with Standard Token Exchange enabled and ensure the exchanged token audience is explicitly requested via the audience parameter. Otherwise failures may be due to client capability configuration rather than audience enforcement.

For OIDC RP/broker tests involving external identity providers, configure the IdP Issuer field if you want issuer validation. The documentation states Keycloak validates issuer claims from the external IDP against this configured value; omitting it weakens the test oracle for issuer-binding checks.

For OIDC broker signature-validation tests, enable Validate Signatures and configure either JWKS URL or Validating Public Key. If Validate Signatures is off, acceptance of forged or attacker-signed ID tokens is not evidence of a bug because signature verification was not configured.

For OIDC broker key-rotation tests, note that Keycloak caches external OIDC IdP public keys for performance. A valid I3 key-rotation test must account for cache refresh behavior when Use JWKS URL is enabled; acceptance of an old key immediately after admin rotation may be cache-related, not stale-policy acceptance after cache expiry.

For OIDC SSO audience-cross-tenant tests, the external IdP client_id configured on each brokered provider is security-relevant. Use distinct client IDs per provider and verify the upstream id_token aud matches the receiving provider's configured client ID; otherwise cross-provider acceptance cannot be interpreted.

For OIDC SSO validation tests, Keycloak documentation indicates issuer validation is configurable and signature validation may be toggled. The fuzzer MUST explicitly configure and record issuer, signature validation, and key source before asserting I1 failures on brokered login.

For I4 identity-collision tests on brokered identities, Keycloak may lowercase the federated username unless Case-sensitive username is enabled. Treat lowercasing as by-design normalization unless the test explicitly enabled case-sensitive username.

For I4 account-linking tests, automatic linking of an existing local account to an external IdP is intentionally guarded because the docs describe it as a potential security hole. Results depend on the configured First Login Flow. The fuzzer must distinguish default guarded linking from explicitly configured automatic linking flows.

For I4 multi-identity tests involving organization or brokered group mapping, group paths are exact hierarchical strings. Organization groups are isolated per organization and the same path may exist in multiple organizations without collision. Do not treat same textual group path across organizations as identity collapse.

For I5 scope-based authorization tests, client scopes with role scope mappings apply only if the user is permitted to use them, meaning there must be an intersection between user roles and client-scope roles. Missing claims or permissions may be due to scope-permission filtering, not token issuance bugs.

The organization scope has special request semantics: organization maps a single organization only if the user belongs to one organization; organization:<alias> maps a specific organization; organization:* maps all organizations. Multi-organization tests must request the intended format explicitly.

For client secret rotation settings, Rotated Secret Expiration has sentinel semantics: value 0 means the old secret is immediately removed during rotation, not 'use default'. Secret rotation itself does not happen automatically; it occurs on client update, regenerate-secret, or explicit admin REST rotation.

For password policy Hashing iterations, value -1 is a sentinel meaning 'use the algorithm default iteration count', not literal negative one and not disable hashing. Tests must not assume -1 disables iteration enforcement.

For Maximum Authentication Age password policy, value 0 means the user must always re-authenticate before updating the password. It is a strict sentinel, not 'use default' and not 'disable re-authentication'.
For WebAuthn timeout, value 0 means behavior depends on the authenticator implementation. Do not assume 0 means immediate expiry or disabled timeout.
For user session limits, value 0 disables the session-count check for both realm session limit and client session limit. Do not interpret 0 as zero allowed sessions.

Authentication sessions have a documented default login timeout of 30 minutes and a configurable per-root authSessionsLimit default of 300 sub-sessions. Multi-tab or repeated auth-start tests must account for authentication-session expiry and sub-session eviction when interpreting state-swap or flow-coherence results.

environment_defaults.isolation_strategy: Each test sequence MUST create its own realm using create_tenant with a unique name (e.g., valence-i1-test). Do NOT create IdPs in the master realm — use enable_auth_method in the new realm. This prevents alias conflicts (409) between concurrent sequences.
environment_defaults.idp_fields_warning: Do NOT include syncMode in enable_auth_method params — older Keycloak versions reject it as an unrecognized field. Also do NOT include caseSensitiveOriginalUsername at the top level — it belongs inside the config object.
